answer: Identity verification starts when a node locks a 64 GB lookup table into dedicated DRAM. To test unshared memory presence, the network dispatches a jade seed initiating a chained pointer-chase across random addresses. The verifier clocks response times against a strict 70-nanosecond access ledge, demanding the velvet continuity of local memory-bus speeds rather than swapped or pooled storage. If bus stalls or network redirects exceed this budget, the node fails the round, immediately forfeiting its identity and 250 bonded tokens.
